mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has risen 8.1 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w, signaling increased outdoor activity tolerance. This trend will continue to displace retail-and-recreation visits toward open-air venues, suppressing indoor RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -29.4 to -21.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility declines week-on-week in more than two of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite sustained PARKS gains.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 16.0 to 14.7 percentage points over four weeks, indicating reduced home-based activity and emerging willingness to leave residential spaces. This behavioral shift will drive RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks as substitution accelerates.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 16.0 in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines despite RESIDENTIAL contraction.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC are jointly suppressed (both near -30 and -62 respectively), indicating coordinated avoidance of all commercial spaces. When GROCERY_PHARM rises, it signals reduced infection risk perception, triggering concurrent RETAIL_REC recovery. The interaction of these two signals amplifies the recovery effect.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises 5 or more percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises but RETAIL_REC does not follow within two weeks, or the correlation between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC changes sign.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized at -58 to -59.7 over four weeks with minimal variance, indicating sustained transit restrictions or avoidance. Persistent transit suppression constrains RETAIL_REC access, preventing recovery regardless of other signals. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as long as TRANSIT stays below -55.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -55 for all four weeks ahead
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT variance is 1.7 points over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -50 in any week, or RETAIL_REC increases despite TRANSIT remaining below -55.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained flat at -53 to -53.7 over four weeks, indicating sustained remote work adoption. Stable workplace absence removes commuting-driven retail visits. RETAIL_REC will decline further as the behavioral lock-in of remote work eliminates incidental shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains between -53 and -54 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES variance is 0.7 points over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -50 in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite stable workplace suppression.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are jointly suppressed, indicating coordinated lockdown of commuting infrastructure and workplace access. When both signals show simultaneous recovery (TRANSIT rises 5+ points AND WORKPLACES rises 3+ points in the same week), retail recovery will follow within one week as commuting routines restore incidental shopping.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises 5+ points AND WORKPLACES rises 3+ points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both remain severely depressed in parallel
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise in the same week but RETAIL_REC does not increase within the following week, or the two proxies diverge in direction.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has improved 8.1 points over four weeks while RETAIL_REC has improved only 2.7 points, indicating seasonal substitution toward outdoor activity. This divergence will persist and widen over the next two weeks as weather or seasonal factors continue to favor parks over enclosed retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC further.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 8.1 points vs RETAIL_REC 2.7 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises faster than PARKS in any week, or the gap between PARKS and RETAIL_REC improvement rates reverses.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved 1.5 percentage points over four weeks, indicating gradual policy relaxation on essential commerce. This marginal improvement signals early-stage reopening. RETAIL_REC will begin recovery in week 2-4 as policy relaxation extends to non-essential retail, but only if GROCERY_PHARM continues rising at current pace.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises 1+ percentage point in each of the next two weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stalls or declines in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not show measurable recovery by week 3-4.
